ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the coordinates of points $A$ and $B$ are $(2,0)$ and $(0,-4)$, respectively. If segment $AB$ is rotated $90^\circ$ clockwise around point $A$ to obtain segment $AC$, then what are the coordinates of point $C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw CD $\perp$ x-axis at point D,\\
$\because$ The coordinates of points A and B are (2, 0) and (0, -4) respectively,\\
$\therefore$ OA=2, OB=4,\\
From the property of rotation, we get: $\angle BAC=90^\circ$, AC=AB,\\
$\because$ $\angle ADC=\angle AOB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CAD=\angle B$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ACD \cong \triangle BAO$,\\
$\therefore$ CD=OA=2, AD=BO=4,\\
$\therefore$ OD=AD−OA=2,\\
$\therefore$ The coordinates of point C are $\boxed{(-2, 2)}$.
